## F002 closure

Every iteration of the prime loop now calls `occurrence()` independently (`crates/daemon/src/idle_nudge.rs:290-307`). The resulting FYI ID uses that fresh 16-byte OS-random part, not the holder nudge's part or a value shared across primes.

The holder ID and earlier FYI IDs remain observable, but they no longer determine a later sibling ID. The new part is used only for its own hold, whose identifying event follows the row's commit. This closes both holder-to-prime and prime-to-prime preemption from the shared occurrence. It relies on OS randomness and 128-bit unpredictability, not a guarantee that random values can never collide.

The two-project/two-prime regression requires both FYIs held, checks their expected seat/anchor/prime shape and 32-character parts, and proves each differs from the known nudge part and from the other FYI. Source formatting establishes lowercase hex; this is not a live exploit/interleaving or cryptographic test.

Author receipts `m224r3.py`, `m224r3.out` and `m224r3-baseline.out` show the eight-case positive baseline and two valid kills: reusing the nudge part and sharing one new part among all primes. Each mutant returns exit 101 and fails the intended regression; seven other cases pass. No reviewer-owned mutant was executed.

## Failure behavior and retained notes

A failed holder draw still marks nothing. A failed **prime** draw occurs after the mark, holds nothing for that prime, records an error in its outcome/audit, and continues to other primes. This is the packet's explicit fail-closed disposition, not durable retry or guaranteed fanout. RNG-failure injection remains unexercised.

The sender-only FYI collision comparison and duplicate-anchor insert-loser path remain source-inspected, as recorded in the previous verdict. Other predictable daemon notice namespaces remain outside this repair. No changes were made to the atomic veto, partial indexes, owner-scoped background reads, generic FYI conflict refusal/audit, labels or plan-222 suppression.
